contributions.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED (39,943.31) on the p2 Summary Page, which is also the filer's own ledger's printed and BOXED 'TOTAL 39,943.31' at the foot of p3, and is re-stated at summary line 4
contributions.detail: The p3 ledger's 13 priced donor rows sum to 3000.00 + 2500.00 + 250.00 + 155.00 + 130.31 + 100.00 + 100.00 + 100.00 + 50.00 + 50.00 + 50.00 + 50.00 + 50.00 = 6,585.31. Adding the block aggregate 308.00 gives 6,893.31; adding the filer's own 'Loan to self' 30,400.00 gives 37,293.31; adding the two IN-KIND rows 150.00 + 2,500.00 gives 39,943.31 EXACTLY = the ledger's own boxed TOTAL = the cover's promoted PER-PERIOD Column A cell. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' is LEFT WHOLLY EMPTY on this cover (both cells blank — not nil marks), so there is nothing cumulative to confuse it with. The p2 ladder closes on its own terms: line 3 2,168.13 + line 4 39,943.31 = line 5 42,111.44; 42,111.44 - line 6 39,552.43 = line 7 2,559.01. THE CLOSURE IS WHAT DECIDES TWO CLASSIFICATIONS: the loan is a contribution row here (line 3 is already occupied by a different figure), and in-kind is counted INLINE (monetary-only stops at 37,293.31, which appears nowhere on the document).

expenditures.anchor: the filer's own ledger's printed 'Total 39,552.43' at the foot of p5, which is also Column A 'Total this Period' TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE (39,552.43) on the p2 Summary Page and summary line 6
expenditures.detail: TRACED, UNIQUE BY CONTIGUITY, and nothing nudged (§C5 / ADDENDUM D §D5 — the spreadsheet SUM-RANGE SLIP class). All 56 rows of the filer's own two-sheet expenses ledger sum to 42,058.99, which is 2,506.56 MORE than the printed Total of 39,552.43. The 43 rows on the FIRST sheet (p4) sum to 39,552.43 EXACTLY — to the cent, over 43 rows — and the 13 rows on the SECOND sheet (p5) sum to exactly the 2,506.56 difference. So the filer's SUM range covers the first sheet only and omits the whole of the second, and the omitted rows are a CONTIGUOUS BLOCK (the entire continuation page), which makes the attribution unique. A second, independent tell inside the same document points the same way: the main ledger is in date order, while the 13 omitted rows run 4/10, 4/10, 4/17, 4/27, 5/2, 5/2, 5/8, 5/9, 5/12, 3/4, 3/6, 3/18, 3/18 — out of order, i.e. appended below the summed range after it was written. The delta is retained verbatim, all 56 rows are published, and the published figure was not changed. NOT SCREENED FOR CORRELATION ACROSS FILINGS: this filer's other 2014 reports are outside this chunk and were not opened, so the one-off-vs-habit question is left open for the coordinator; the attribution inside this document does not depend on it.

in_kind_convention: MONETARY-PLUS-IN-KIND, INLINE — a per-filer departure from the legacy_colAB family default, and both conventions were tested. The filer heads a block 'In Kind' at the foot of his contributions ledger and prices both of its entries (150.00 'Beef' and 2,500.00 'Signs') in the same Amount column as his cash rows. Monetary-only gives 37,293.31, which matches NOTHING printed anywhere on the filing; monetary-plus-in-kind gives 39,943.31, which is simultaneously the ledger's own boxed TOTAL and the cover's Column A. In-kind counted is what closes it. (Contrast the Stanley filing in this same chunk and cycle, whose footnote excludes in-kind — the treatment really is per filer.)
escalation_note: Thirteen 900 dpi --value amount-cell crops (p3 rows 1, 13, 14, 49, 50, 53 and the line past the last row; p4 rows 1, 43 and the line past; p5 rows 1, 13 and the line past) plus two ~500-700 dpi block strips over p3's Name/Last/City columns to confirm 49 donor spellings on a faxed page. No figure was in dispute: every one of the three sheet totals closes on the page's own printed figure or is traced in recon.

3.measure_note: THIS PAGE IS NOT A COUNTY FORM — it is the filer's own typed portrait ledger substituted for Schedule A (ADDENDUM E §E5 / A §A2), and rowbands.py returns ZERO printed rules on it. Geometry recovered by the sanctioned route: `rowbands.py <pdf> 3 --text-lines --col` run twice, once over the Name column (5-25) and once over the Amount column (84-94). The name-column scan returns 56 text bands = fax header + title + column header + 49 DATA ROWS (11.72 .. 82.95, even pitch 1.485) + the loan row 84.54 + the 'In Kind' heading 87.94 + two in-kind rows 89.49 and 90.77; the amount-column scan independently returns bands at the same 13 priced rows and at 82.96 / 84.42 / 89.46 / 90.87 / 92.32, agreeing with the name column to within 0.12 pct. Bands are [top-0.30, top+1.20]. The 51st band is the 'In Kind' HEADING: it publishes no row but CONSUMES an index (ADDENDUM E §E3), which is why the in-kind rows are 52 and 53. `cells` are read off the printed column headings (Name / Last / Street / Suite / City / State / Zip / Amount) and are approximate on this ruleless page; the AMOUNT band is the measured one. CONTROLS at 900 dpi --value: (1) §A1 FIRST-ENTRY CONTROL — band 1 pct:84.0,11.42,9.5,1.50@p3 RENDERED '3,000.00' (row 1 as recorded), so the ledger's first written entry really is band 1; (2) band 13 RENDERED '50.00'; (3) band 14 RENDERED an EMPTY cell — the internal control that proves the un-priced block starts exactly there and that the 36 blank amounts are the document's, not a frame error; (4) band 49 RENDERED '308.00'; (5) band 50 RENDERED '30,400.00'; (6) the LAST row, band 53, RENDERED '2,500.00'; (7) ONE LINE PAST THE LAST ROW, pct:84.0,92.02,9.5,1.50@p3, RENDERED the ledger's own BOXED TOTAL '39,943.31' rather than a 54th entry — proving the frame is not short by one.

4.measure_note: The filer's own typed expenses ledger, sheet 1 — a boxed HEADER row (Date / Vender / Mailing Address / Amount) but NO printed row rules, so rowbands.py finds only 4 rules. Geometry recovered with `--text-lines --col`: the Amount column (78-90) returns 44 text bands = the 'Amount' header at 13.87 plus 43 DATA ROWS at 15.60 .. 90.01, even pitch 1.772; the Date/Vender column (8-30) independently returns the same 44 lines offset by ~0.2 pct. Bands are [top-0.30, top+1.20]. CONTROLS at 900 dpi --value: (1) §A1 FIRST-ENTRY CONTROL — band 1 pct:78.0,15.30,12.0,1.77@p4 RENDERED '1,500.00' with the printed header rule above it, so the first entry is band 1 and the header line is correctly excluded; (2) the LAST row, band 43, RENDERED '482.96'; (3) §B5 NEGATIVE CONTROL one line past it, pct:78.0,91.48,12.0,1.77@p4, RENDERED an EMPTY area — the sheet ends at row 43 and continues on p5.

5.measure_note: Sheet 2 of the same typed ledger — no header row of its own, no printed rules, the rows simply continue. `--text-lines --col 78,90` returns 15 bands = the fax header line plus 13 DATA ROWS at 9.65 .. 30.92 (pitch 1.772, identical to sheet 1) plus the ledger's printed 'Total' line at 32.69; the Date/Vender scan returns the same 13 rows. Bands are [top-0.30, top+1.20]. CONTROLS at 900 dpi --value: (1) §A1 FIRST-ENTRY CONTROL — band 1 pct:78.0,9.35,12.0,1.77@p5 RENDERED '638.00' (row 1 as recorded), so no line was skipped at the top of the continuation sheet; (2) the LAST row, band 13, RENDERED '16.32'; (3) ONE LINE PAST THE LAST ROW, pct:78.0,32.39,12.0,1.77@p5, RENDERED the ledger's printed Total '39,552.43' rather than a 14th entry — which is also the figure the recon delta is measured against.
